answer: Before sunrise the well keeper lowers the knotted rope and reads the water's depth, and the figure goes into the well book before anyone may draw. A karst depth guessed from yesterday fails the rope: at the juniper of the well the knots must show where the water truly stands, and a guessed figure leaves the caravan thirsty by noon. Forging the readings means bribing the keeper, faking 240 dawns of measures and paying 8,900, while the pearl entry in the well book is read at every watering, so water whose depth was never measured is refused to the liar.
